source_text: [1] Οὐ διατάσσομαι ὑμῖν ὡς ὤν τις. εἰ γὰρ καὶ δέδεμαι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι, οὔπω ἀπήρτισμαι ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ: νῦν γὰρ ἀρχὴν ἔχω τοῦ μαθητεύεσθαι, καὶ προσλαλῶ ὑμῖν ὡς συνδιδασκαλίταις μου. ἐμὲ γὰρ ἔδει ὑφ̓ ὑμῶν ὑπαλειφθῆναι πίστει, νουθεσίᾳ, ὑπομονῇ, μακροθυμίᾳ. [2] ἀλλ’ ἐπεὶ ἡ ἀγάπη οὐκ ἐᾷ με σιωπᾶν περὶ ὑμῶν, διὰ τοῦτο προέλαβον παρακαλεῖν ὑμᾶς, ὅπως συντρέχητε τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὸ ἀδιάκριτον ἡμῶν ζῆν, τοῦ πατρὸς ἡ γνώμη, ὡς καὶ οἱ ἐπίσκοποι, οἱ κατὰ τὰ πέρατα ὁρισθέντες, ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ γνώμῃ εἰσίν.
pass_a_gloss: I do not give you orders as if I were someone. For even if I am in chains for the Name, I have not yet been made perfect in Jesus Christ. For now I have a beginning of being a disciple, and I speak to you as my fellow learners. For I ought to have been anointed by you, as an athlete is, with faith, admonition, endurance, and patience. But since love does not let me be silent about you, therefore I have taken the lead in urging you to run together with the mind of God. For Jesus Christ too, our inseparable life, is the mind of the Father, just as the bishops, appointed in the farthest parts of the earth, are in the mind of Jesus Christ.

lemmas.gloss: anoint, rub with oil (as athletes before a contest)

pass_b_english: I am not giving you orders as though I were somebody. I am in chains for the Name, yes, but I have not yet been made perfect in Jesus Christ. I am only now beginning to be a disciple, and I speak to you as my fellow students. It is I who needed you to anoint me like an athlete for the contest, with faith, with warning, with endurance, with patience.

But love will not let me keep quiet about you. So I have stepped forward first to urge you: run in step with the mind of God. For Jesus Christ, our inseparable life, is the Father's mind. In the same way the bishops, appointed to the farthest ends of the earth, are in the mind of Jesus Christ.

choices.english: anoint me like an athlete for the contest
choices.why: ὑπαλείφω is the oil rub before a match; Ignatius pictures himself as a wrestler about to fight the beasts.
γνώμη is mind, purpose, or will; 'mind' keeps the run-together-with-the-bishop's-mind chain of Eph 3-4 intact.
rejected: the [manifested] will of the Father (ANF; adds 'manifested')

choices.why: ἀδιάκριτος: undivided, not to be separated from us.
τις used of a person of importance; colloquial 'somebody' carries it.
rejected: as if I were some great person (ANF; wordier)

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned. ANF 'stirred up' loses the athlete's anointing in ὑπαλειφθῆναι, and '[manifested] will' supplies a word not in the Greek.

notes: Whole chapter 3 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
The 'run together with the mind' chain continues into chapter 4 (συντρέχειν τῇ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου γνώμῃ); English kept consistent with ignatius_ephesians_4.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked clause by clause. Οὐ διατάσσομαι ὑμῖν ὡς ὤν τις matches Pass A “I do not give you orders as if I were someone” and Pass B “I am not giving you orders as though I were somebody.” εἰ γὰρ καὶ δέδεμαι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι, οὔπω ἀπήρτισμαι ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ is kept as chains for the Name plus “not yet been made perfect.” νῦν γὰρ ἀρχὴν ἔχω τοῦ μαθητεύεσθαι and συνδιδασκαλίταις μου are the beginning of discipleship and fellow learners/students. ἐμὲ γὰρ ἔδει ὑφ̓ ὑμῶν ὑπαλειφθῆναι πίστει, νουθεσίᾳ, ὑπομονῇ, μακροθυμίᾳ keeps you as agents and all four datives; the athlete gloss follows the supplied ὑπαλείφω lemma. ἡ ἀγάπη οὐκ ἐᾷ με σιωπᾶν περὶ ὑμῶν and ὅπως συντρέχητε τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ are preserved. Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὸ ἀδιάκριτον ἡμῶν ζῆν, τοῦ πατρὸς ἡ γνώμη is “our inseparable life” and the Father’s mind; οἱ ἐπίσκοποι … ὁρισθέντες … ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ γνώμῃ εἰσίν stay passive and “in the mind of Jesus Christ.” No scripture is quoted and no citation is added or shifted. Title “Christ, the Father's mind” names the thought.

Paragraph 1: Greek source matches Ignatius Ephesians 3. Pass A renders all clauses: negation in Οὐ διατάσσομαι ὑμῖν ὡς ὤν τις → 'I do not give you orders as if I were someone' (preserves agency and negation); εἰ γὰρ καὶ δέδεμαι... οὔπω ἀπήρτισμαι → 'For even if I am in chains for the Name, I have not yet been made perfect' (preserves concession, negation, agency); νῦν γὰρ ἀρχὴν ἔχω τοῦ μαθητεύεσθαι → 'For now I have a beginning of being a disciple' (preserves agency and aspect); προσλαλῶ ὑμῖν ὡς συνδιδασκαλίταις μου → 'I speak to you as my fellow learners' (preserves agency and comparison); ἐμὲ γὰρ ἔδει ὑφ̓ ὑμῶν ὑπαλειφθῆναι... → 'For I ought to have been anointed by you... with faith, admonition, endurance, and patience' (preserves passive agency, qualification, and list); ἀλλ’ ἐπεὶ ἡ ἀγάπη οὐκ ἐᾷ με σιωπᾶν... → 'But since love does not let me be silent about you...' (preserves negation, agency, modality); διὰ τοῦτο προέλαβον παρακαλεῖν... ὅπως συντρέχητε τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ → 'therefore I have taken the lead in urging you to run together with the mind of God' (preserves agency, purpose, and dative); καὶ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὸ ἀδιάκριτον ἡμῶν ζῆν, τοῦ πατρὸς ἡ γνώμη... → 'For Jesus Christ too, our inseparable life, is the mind of the Father' (preserves apposition, identity, and genitive); ὡς καὶ οἱ ἐπίσκοποι... ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ γνώμῃ εἰσίν → 'just as the bishops... are in the mind of Jesus Christ' (preserves comparison and agency). Pass B: first sentence matches Pass A and Greek on negation, agency, concession, and aspect; second sentence matches on agency, purpose, and identity. No omitted clauses, qualifications, or repetitions. Title 'Christ, the Father's mind' names the thought (the identity of Christ as divine mind). No uncertainties. Covered source paragraph: [1].
